neighbours.label: the count or article right after a scoring verb in an American-football report (scored two / score a / kicked three), where a tally of touchdowns or points comes next
fire: Late in the game the Falcons scored two touchdowns to take the lead.
In the opening half the Broncos scored four touchdowns against a tired defense.
With a minute left, the Vikings needed to score a touchdown from midfield.
On a rainy Sunday the Saints scored 28 points in the second half.
After the turnover the Chargers scored three straight times on long drives.
Despite the injury, Ohio State scored five touchdowns in the first half.
Trailing by ten, the Titans kicked two field goals in the last quarter.
Behind their young quarterback the Jets scored 35 points in the win.
quiet: Before the kickoff the Falcons called two meetings to rest the defense.
In training camp the Broncos lost four linemen to a stomach bug.
A minute later, the Vikings tried to find a receiver near midfield.
The Saints signed 28 jerseys for fans after a rainy practice on Sunday.
Coming out of the huddle the Chargers ran three straight plays up the middle.
For the opener, Ohio State started five seniors on the offensive line.
Short on depth, the Titans sent two backup tackles into the huddle.
Their young quarterback helped the Jets draw 35 thousand fans to the stadium.

notes: Card's top example is 'scored three touchdowns'. Probes: 'scored 21' and 'kicked three' fire, 'bought three apples' and 'scored three points on the math test' do not. The card's non-sports examples (': Allen & Unwin', 'the classical') did not reproduce, so this may be partial.
